population: A fixed, synthetic set of ten atomic mathematical and inferential claims; not a sampled population of deployed AI answers.

sources.scope: Published existence theorem only; the full proof mechanism was not authenticated for this fixture.
Documents a proposed uniqueness conjecture and its argument; not proof of uniqueness.
Integer polynomial identity, cubic discriminants, and circumference formula reproducible by the accompanying standard-library test; no independent reviewer.

cases.claim: A regular 11-gon is constructible by marked ruler and compass.
cases.reason: The publisher's abstract states the proved existence theorem.

cases.claim: For a unit-side regular 11-gon, R=1/(2 sin(pi/11)) approximately 1.7747327664.
cases.reason: Elementary regular-polygon geometry; numerical display is deterministically checked.
Correct polynomial identity in characteristic 11, not over the real numbers.

cases.claim: A repeated root of the cubic modulo 11 proves the cubic has a repeated root over the real numbers.
cases.reason: Its characteristic-zero discriminant is -44000, not zero; reduction modulo a prime does not preserve this conclusion.

cases.claim: The conjecture's cubic 25r^3-40r^2+21r-2 has the unit-side hendecagon circumradius as a root.
cases.reason: At R=1/(2 sin(pi/11)), the polynomial evaluates to approximately 49.02818, not zero.

cases.claim: Eleven is the only non-Pierpont prime for which a regular polygon is constructible by marked ruler and compass.
cases.reason: The published result establishes existence for 11, while the later source offers a conjecture, not a universal impossibility theorem.

cases.claim: Failure of one attempted construction method for 31-, 41-, and 61-gons proves that every marked-ruler construction of those polygons is impossible.
cases.reason: Failure of a particular approach is not a proof about every possible method.

cases.claim: The cited constructibility results establish an improvement in cryptographic security.
cases.reason: No cryptographic threat model, construction, or evidence is supplied.

cases.claim: The polynomial u^3+2u^2+2u+2 and 25r^3-40r^2+21r-2 are literally the same polynomial.
cases.reason: They have different coefficient sequences and discriminants (-44 versus -44000); any other relationship needs separate derivation.

cases.claim: Cubing is a bijection on the finite field F_11.
cases.reason: The multiplicative group of nonzero residues has order 10 and gcd(3,10)=1; this is not an explanation of cubic root multiplicity.
